answer: When power flow reverses on an interconnector, the reversal second is logged by both grid operators, so a claimant reports the reversal it observed in local frequency and its samples must match the operators' log. A single matching sample is not enough, so the verifier checks a full minute around the reversal, including the frequency wobble that follows it; no oasis of calm data can hide a missing wobble, a garden of copied readings fails, and the reversal is felt only at the inlet where the two grids meet, so a farm claiming distant feeders cannot reproduce it.
